rows.title: Analysis: A digital divide with dire consequences for Texas
rows.standfirst: The new coronavirus has forced Texans online for education, commerce, work and entertainment. But a third of the state’s residents don’t have broadband in their homes.

rows.title: She says she needs an abortion. Texas is citing coronavirus to stop her.
rows.standfirst: Heather Artrip is one of hundreds of Texans whose plans regarding reproductive health have been cast into uncertainty in the wake of an executive order from Gov. Greg Abbott barring any procedures that are not “immediately medically necessary.”

rows.title: Rent is due. But thousands of Texans have lost their jobs because of the coronavirus pandemic.
rows.standfirst: Evictions across the state are halted until at least April 20, thanks to a Texas Supreme Court moratorium. But both renters and landlords are worried about what comes next.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/1: El Paso strengthens stay-at-home order
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Some local elections in Texas moving ahead despite coronavirus spread
rows.standfirst: A few small towns and water districts aren’t canceling their May 2 elections despite fears of infection spreading at polling places. But it appears most cities across Texas have pushed their elections back to November.

rows.title: TribCast: The politics of coronavirus in Texas
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Ross, Emma and Jolie about Gov. Greg Abbott’s response to the coronavirus outbreak, the newest front in the state’s fight against abortion and the state vs. local battle over bail.

rows.title: Texas schools are paying support staff; work for substitute teachers dries up
rows.standfirst: With schools closed statewide to halt the spread of the new coronavirus, hourly workers like custodians and bus drivers worry how long their paychecks will keep coming. Substitute teachers aren’t finding paid work at all.

rows.title: Thousands in Texas face delays to their unemployment relief because of busy phone lines and website outages
rows.standfirst: As tens of thousands of Texans try to file unemployment insurance claims, they’re finding the Texas Workforce Commission’s phone lines jammed and website servers overloaded as the agency is swamped by the crush of sudden need.

rows.title: Inmates’ attorneys challenge Gov. Greg Abbott’s order banning some jail releases, say it’s unconstitutional
rows.standfirst: Plaintiffs in an ongoing Harris County lawsuit over felony bail practices are asking a federal judge to temporarily block Abbott’s order.

rows.title: Local governments, already hard hit by the coronavirus, are facing a fresh budget threat: economic recession
rows.standfirst: Cities are projecting decreases in sales tax revenue, one of their most important financial sources. How bad the losses are — and what will have to be cut — depends on how long the pandemic lasts.

rows.title: Lack of rapid coronavirus tests hinders care for respiratory patients, emergency doctors say
rows.standfirst: Without rapid testing available in hospitals and ambulances, doctors, nurses and respiratory therapists are left to make difficult decisions about patients with other conditions who are struggling to breathe.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/2: More than a quarter million Texans file for unemployment relief in one week
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: The number of Texans filing for unemployment has soared 1,600% in two weeks
rows.standfirst: Last week alone, 275,597 out-of-work Texans filed for unemployment relief.

rows.title: Expecting a rush of COVID-19 patients, hospitals prepare their most important resource: health care workers
rows.standfirst: With elective procedures canceled, hospitals are reassigning staff. But even the best-laid plans may go awry if clinicians fall ill in large numbers.

rows.title: Despite coronavirus risks, some Texas religious groups are worshipping in person — with the governor’s blessing
rows.standfirst: COVID-19 has spread rapidly in Texas, and many congregations closed their doors and moved religious services online. But there are some religious groups who say it’s their right to remain open because they believe they provide an essential service to their communities.

rows.title: “A church is hands on”: Why these Texas churches aren’t closing their doors
rows.standfirst: As religious groups across the state move their services online in response to COVID-19 and local governments mandate stay-at-home orders, there are still some who say in-person gatherings are an integral part of their faith.

rows.title: Candidate jolts battleground congressional race with ad blasting China for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The ad from Republican Kathaleen Wall says China “poisoned our people” with the coronavirus. The Democratic nominee for the seat, Sri Preston Kulkarni, denounced it as “race-baiting.”

rows.title: Texas tells locals they must delay their upcoming May elections
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott previously paved the way for municipalities to push their May elections to November. But a handful of small towns and special districts hadn’t canceled despite fears of infection spreading at polling places.

rows.title: Coronavirus outbreak at Texas City nursing home follows cluster of patients at San Antonio facility
rows.standfirst: Officials in both regions are tracking the movements of nursing home staffers, many of whom work at multiple facilities.

rows.title: Analysis: It’s still religion even if you’re not congregating in person
rows.standfirst: To help keep the new coronavirus at bay, Gov. Greg Abbott wants us to stay away from each other, but he made an exception for church services. That was a critical mistake during the 1918 flu pandemic. It still is.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/3: Harris County has 1,000 infected residents; CDC now recommends cloth face coverings in public
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott address hospital capacity in the wake of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Watch the Texas governor discuss hospitals’ response to patients diagnosed with COVID-19, the disease caused by the new coronavirus. Abbott is set to speak live at 2:30 p.m. Central time.

rows.title: Along the border, the population is high risk for coronavirus, but testing is in short supply
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott promised that all those who need a coronavirus test “will get one,” but near the border tests are scarce, and the death toll is beginning to rise.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott isn’t calling it a stay-at-home order. But he’s telling Texans to stay at home.
rows.standfirst: The order “requires all Texans to stay at home except to provide essential services or do essential things like going to the grocery store,” Abbott said this week.

rows.title: Hundreds of UT-Austin students went to Cabo San Lucas for spring break. Nearly 50 have coronavirus.
rows.standfirst: The number of students with positive tests continues to grow as the University of Texas at Austin is now aware of 211 students who traveled to Cabo San Lucas for Spring Break.

rows.title: Led by science, Clay Jenkins pushed Dallas County virus response ahead of Texas
rows.standfirst: Dallas County Judge Clay Jenkins decided early on not to be timid in his response to the coronavirus. He moved quickly to shut down the nation’s eighth most populous county, and prodded other counties and Gov. Greg Abbott to follow along.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/4: Officials investigate San Antonio nursing home experiencing outbreak
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/5: State reports 6,812 cases and 127 deaths
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Health care workers on the front lines of coronavirus don’t get expanded paid sick leave protections
rows.standfirst: The Labor Department has urged employers to “be judicious” in exempting their workers. Critics say the exemption hurts nurses and doctors, who have already complained about their lack of protective equipment.

rows.title: Analysis: What makes a business essential depends on where you sit
rows.standfirst: Nonessential businesses in Texas (and elsewhere) have been told to close — a measure intended to increase social distance and to slow the spread of the new coronavirus. But every business is essential to someone.

rows.title: Why COVID-19 is so dangerous
rows.standfirst: World-renowned scientist Dr. Peter Hotez talks straight with Texas A&M System Chancellor John Sharp about the extreme difficulties ahead.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott deliver the latest on efforts to contain the coronavirus in Texas
rows.standfirst: With nearly 7,000 confirmed cases of COVID-19 as of Sunday, Abbott will relay what the state is doing to contain the spread of the infectious disease. Watch live starting at 2 p.m. Central.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/6: 7,276 cases and 140 deaths; state opens checkpoints near Louisiana border
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas City nursing home residents with coronavirus being treated with unproven hydroxychloroquine drug
rows.standfirst: The physician and nursing home medical director who prescribed the drug is a campaign surrogate for President Donald Trump.

rows.title: As oil price crisis grips the globe, small Texas producers feel the ripple effects
rows.standfirst: Plummeting demand and an international price dispute have forced Texas oil producers to begin shutting wells.

rows.title: Texas’ small-business owners tap patience and experts to navigate coronavirus relief options
rows.standfirst: Companies trying to prevent layoffs are turning to banks, accountants and nonprofits to help them apply for federal assistance during the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: UT-Austin President Greg Fenves leaving Texas flagship June 30 for Emory University
rows.standfirst: University of Texas officials confirmed the departure on Tuesday morning.

rows.title: The Texas real estate market is headed for a slowdown. The question is for how long.
rows.standfirst: Experts are concerned for regions like Houston and the Permian Basin, which might feel the economic effects not only of the pandemic, but also of the low price of oil.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/7: State reports 8,262 cases and 154 deaths; 5 more die at San Antonio nursing home
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: ER Doc: “Let us help!”
rows.standfirst: As Texas mobilizes to fight a pandemic, over 200 licensed ERs – staffed with thousands of emergency doctors and nurses, equipped with ventilators, labs, and pharmacies – aren’t part of the plan yet.

rows.title: Cancel chemo or risk compromised immune system? Cancer patients and oncologists confront coronavirus challenges
rows.standfirst: To combat coronavirus, hospitals and medical providers were told to cancel procedures and surgeries that aren’t urgent. But cancer patients facing delayed chemotherapy treatments say the stakes are higher for them.

rows.title: Texas Democrats again sue to ease vote-by-mail rules during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: The Texas Democratic Party is asking both federal and state courts to rule on whether any voter in upcoming elections should be able to ask for an absentee ballot to mail in and avoid possible infection at polling places.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas cities: See how social distancing could reduce stress on hospitals
rows.standfirst: New estimates from University of Texas at Austin researchers show what it would take to spread out hospitalizations in 22 Texas metro areas.

rows.title: Texas can enforce abortion ban during coronavirus pandemic, federal appeals court rules
rows.standfirst: Republican state officials have said barring the procedure in almost all cases is essential for preserving hospital resources during the pandemic. Abortion providers call it political opportunism — and unconstitutional.

rows.title: With Greg Fenves leaving, UT-Austin loses “steady” hand in unsteady times
rows.standfirst: Fenves’ five-year tenure as president brought a sense of stability to the downtown Austin campus. With the coronavirus pandemic upending the university and hammering its budget, his successor will face “trial by ordeal.”

rows.title: Analysis: A fast drop for the Texas economy — and for the state budget
rows.standfirst: The pandemic’s impact on the Texas economy is a full-on recession, state Comptroller Glenn Hegar said Tuesday. And hard financial decisions will mark the next session of the Texas Legislature.

rows.title: Coronavirus is spreading in Texas nursing homes. But the state won’t share the details.
rows.standfirst: Families and advocates for nursing home residents are calling on Texas officials to release the numbers and names of facilities where coronavirus infection has been reported, as other states have done.

rows.title: Food banks rely on donations from grocery stores. But as Texans rush stores, grocers have less to give.
rows.standfirst: Demand for assistance from food banks is off the charts. But volunteers are staying at home, and grocery stores, which typically are key donors to pantries, are seeing their shelves depleted.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/8: Statewide cases top 9,000 with 177 deaths; San Antonio to furlough workers
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott discuss measures taken to address growing number of COVID-19 patients
rows.standfirst: With more than 8,200 cases reported in Texas as of Tuesday, Abbott will discuss the latest in the state’s response to the spread of COVID-19. Watch live starting at noon Central Time.

rows.title: Coronavirus: The pandemic through Texans’ eyes
rows.standfirst: Texas Tribune reporters have interviewed Texans from across the state to learn how they are confronting the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic. Read their stories of struggle and resourcefulness in the first installment of a weekly series.

rows.title: “I feel like I’m pregnant during the apocalypse”: How expectant Texas mothers are navigating the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Expectant mothers across the state are worried about finding baby supplies or giving birth alone. So far, Texas hospitals have sharply restricted their visitor policies, but none have prohibited visitors in delivery rooms.

rows.title: Harris County judges, ACLU sue Greg Abbott over order limiting jail releases during pandemic
rows.standfirst: Misdemeanor judges and criminal defense organizations argue the governor’s order unconstitutionally oversteps his authority over judges and creates a wealth-based detention system. It’s the second court challenge to the order.

rows.title: TribCast: Texas health care workers take on the coronavirus
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Emma and Shannon about how health care workers are preparing for a rush of COVID-19 hospitalizations and why health care workers on the front lines don’t get expanded paid sick leave protections.

rows.title: The first Texas prisoner has died after testing positive for the new coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The death of the 72-year-old man came one day after a 49-year-old correctional officer who worked at a different prison died. The state is locking down 15 prisons where inmates or guards have tested positive for the disease.

rows.title: Impacts of coronavirus on Texans of color clouded by incomplete data
rows.standfirst: The emerging national picture shows black Americans disproportionately getting sick and dying from COVID-19. The same trend may be playing out in Texas’ black and Hispanic communities, but sparse data has been collected.

rows.title: Citing social responsibility, many churches and businesses deemed essential are closing anyway
rows.standfirst: “This is the only way to be sure that we’re not making everybody sicker,” said one restaurant general manager. “We wanted to be able to be an example.”

rows.title: In East Texas, thousands of Easter lilies with no place to go
rows.standfirst: Don Darby’s crop bloomed perfectly this year. But with many churches closed to slow the spread of the new coronavirus, most will never leave his greenhouses.

rows.title: State-run homes for Texans with developmental disabilities aren’t ready for coronavirus outbreaks, some workers warn
rows.standfirst: Officials say they’re ramping up support by providing more testing across Texas and additional personnel for facilities where the virus has been detected. But people close to the facilities have reported that the state is responding too slowly to the emergency.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/9: ACLU sues Dallas County to release inmates over 50
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: More Texans filed for unemployment in the last 4 weeks than all of 2019
rows.standfirst: The numbers are early — but incomplete — indicators of how dramatically and suddenly the state’s economy has collapsed under social distancing orders officials issued to curb the still growing public health crisis spurred by the novel coronavirus.

rows.title: Houston-area lawmakers urge DA to investigate possible “non-existent” March primary candidate
rows.standfirst: “We are concerned that more than 2500 Harris County voters may have been duped,” the Democratic lawmakers wrote.

rows.title: Texas: How has coronavirus changed your life?
rows.standfirst: Our multimedia team is asking Texans to send in a brief video telling us about the day-to-day changes in your life since society essentially shut down last month to limit the spread of the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Some abortions may proceed in Texas during the coronavirus pandemic, federal judge rules
rows.standfirst: In his second rebuke to state officials, U.S. District Judge Lee Yeakel ruled Thursday that certain patients may undergo abortions as Texas battles the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Government watchdog: Millions wasted on Tornillo migrant detention facility
rows.standfirst: The Government Accountability Office found that the government spent $66 million in taxpayer money over five months to hold an average of 28 people per day at the tent encampment near El Paso.

rows.title: More than 13% of Texas nursing homes have at least one resident with coronavirus, officials say
rows.standfirst: The disclosure comes after The Texas Tribune reported Wednesday that Texas was not sharing comprehensive data on nursing homes, as other states have done.

rows.title: Special education students fall behind as Texas schools scramble to adapt
rows.standfirst: Before the coronavirus pandemic, Texas schools were already failing many students with disabilities. School closings have made the job tougher and forced many parents to become amateur special ed teachers.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas has scant data about the pandemic, leaving a lot of questions
rows.standfirst: State officials have a lot more data about the new coronavirus than they did just days ago. But Texas remains behind the curve when it comes to critical information about the spread of the disease.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/10: State reports 11,671 cases and 226 deaths
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott give latest update in state’s response to fighting the spread of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: With nearly 11,700 Texans having tested positive for the new coronavirus, Abbott is set to give an update on the situation. Watch live starting at 2 p.m. Central Time.

rows.title: A Laredo ER spent $500,000 on coronavirus tests. Health officials say they’re unreliable.
rows.standfirst: A private emergency room owner bought 20,000 rapid COVID-19 tests, but a week later they were seized by the federal government. It’s a bitter example of what can go wrong when local governments try to buy supplies on the open market from unknown manufacturers.

rows.title: Federal appeals court once again allows Texas to block many abortions, but allows some pregnant women to proceed
rows.standfirst: Abortion providers said the latest ruling from the federal appeals court leaves abortion “largely inaccessible” in Texas.

rows.title: Texas officials say they see signs that social distancing is slowing the spread of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Top health officials stressed, however, that it’s far too soon to declare victory as the number of Texans infected continues to grow. Gov. Greg Abbott said he’d issue an order next week to lay the groundwork for reopening the state’s economy.

rows.title: Texas banned abortion during the pandemic, but she got one anyway. How the legal battle is creating confusion for clinics
rows.standfirst: The courts volleyed back and forth this week, siding in turns with the state and then with abortion providers. But clinics across the state are responding inconsistently, with some shutting down altogether while they await a final answer.

rows.title: Court blocks Gov. Abbott’s order limiting jail release during pandemic after judges challenged its constitutionality
rows.standfirst: The governor’s order prohibited judges from releasing some inmates without paying bail. The lawsuit filed Wednesday argued it violated the constitutional separation of powers and discriminated against poor defendants.

rows.title: Texas doctors are using plasma from recovered COVID-19 patients to treat others. They’re not yet sure if it will work.
rows.standfirst: The method has been used to treat the sick in past epidemics, and it’s generally considered low risk. Doctors around the nation have started using it on the sickest COVID-19 patients.

rows.title: Limited seating and pajama bottoms: How Texas churches are preparing for a socially distant Easter
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott has given his blessing for churches to hold services during the pandemic. Some are gathering their flocks for Easter. Others are sticking with livestreamed services.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/11: Abortion providers take legal fight to Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas prisons won’t accept new county jail inmates as coronavirus spreads in lockups
rows.standfirst: The Texas Department of Justice sent a letter to county sheriffs announcing the new policy Saturday.

rows.title: Angelo State University president reportedly steps down
rows.standfirst: The university set enrollment records under Brian May, who abruptly resigned, according to KTXS.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court stays lower court ruling, temporarily reviving Gov. Abbott’s order restricting jail release
rows.standfirst: On Friday, a state district judge blocked enforcement of Abbott’s order, which prohibits jail release for some inmates without paying bail during the coronavirus pandemic. She cited unconstitutional provisions and executive overreach as reasons for her order.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas 4/12: More than 13,400 Texans infected, 271 deaths
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Analysis: Is voting in person during a pandemic the best we can do?
rows.standfirst: Texas lawmakers are historically resistant to changing voting practices — and the current coronavirus-inspired push for voting by mail is no exception. But this isn’t just about voting anymore.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Texas reports 13,906 cases and 287 deaths; Austin-area officials mandate face coverings in some instances
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott discuss new plan to help small businesses harmed by coronavirus-related closures
rows.standfirst: As much of the Texas economy remains at a standstill to minimize the spread of the new coronavirus, Abbott will lay out a new program aimed at helping small businesses. Watch it live at 11:30 a.m. Central Time.

rows.title: Pandemic scholars warned U.S. was unprepared
rows.standfirst: Scientists at Bush School talk with Texas A&M System Chancellor John Sharp about COVID-19 and the ignored lessons of SARS, MERS, H1N1 and Ebola.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says reopening the Texas economy will be a slow process
rows.standfirst: He says he’ll outline his plans this week, but it won’t be a “rush-the-gates, everybody-is-able-to-suddenly-reopen-all-at-once” situation.

rows.title: After a beloved principal’s death, Waco middle school community grieves apart
rows.standfirst: Phillip Perry was the leader many believed would rescue a troubled Waco middle school and help its students soar. Two weeks after his death from the coronavirus, students and teachers learn the added pain of mourning during a pandemic.

rows.title: 230,000 Texas families filed for SNAP food assistance in March, twice as many as same month last year
rows.standfirst: Texas has implemented some changes to help Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program recipients, but it hasn’t relaxed eligibility requirements.

rows.title: Texas redistricting could be affected by coronavirus-related delays of census
rows.standfirst: Under a proposal by the Trump administration, the delivery of data Texas lawmakers need to redraw political districts would be pushed to July — past the end of the state’s regular legislative session.

rows.title: Federal appeals court allows medication abortions in Texas during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: The appeals court’s latest ruling comes after abortion providers and state officials have battled over what access to the procedure should be allowed during the public health crisis.

rows.title: Many Texas prisoners have been approved for parole but can’t walk free yet. Advocates say coronavirus should change that.
rows.standfirst: Relatives of Texas prisoners approved for parole question why their loved ones have to stay in disease-prone facilities while completing programs they say could be done virtually and from home.

rows.title: How coronavirus impacted Texas: Hospitalizations, vaccinations, cases and deaths
rows.standfirst: From April 2020 to August 2022, the Texas Tribune used data from the Texas Department of State Health Services to track coronavirus hospitalizations, vaccinations, cases and deaths. We stopped updating these numbers in August 2022.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Hard-line conservatives want stay-at-home order relaxed; Paxton issues opinion on temporary tax exemption
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Texas tax breaks help in disasters — just not public health disasters
rows.standfirst: Property tax exemptions and sales tax holidays only offer savings for events like hurricanes or floods.

rows.title: Baylor University announces up to $80 million in budget cuts in wake of coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: The private school, anticipating a drop in enrollment next school year, is one of the first major Texas colleges to announce budget cuts due to the public health and economic crises.

rows.title: In a pandemic and an election year, Texas Democrats look for the right tone
rows.standfirst: The party, which has high hopes in the state in 2020, is looking to offer contrast without politicizing a crisis.

rows.title: Analysis: What will Texas reopen, and when?
rows.standfirst: The same questions shadow the debates about when to ease coronavirus restrictions on business and social activities and whether to broaden voting by mail in Texas in advance of elections in July and November.

rows.title: Texas school closings fray the personal bonds between teachers and students
rows.standfirst: Karen Sams and Michelle Sandoval, both 2020 Texas Teachers of the Year, know how important it is to see their students in the classrooms and hallways. Without that contact, they fear some are slipping away.

rows.title: Texas’ oil and gas regulators aren’t ready to cut production yet. They’re not even sure how it would work if they did.
rows.standfirst: The Railroad Commission, which oversees the state’s oil and gas industry, took more than 10 hours of testimony about whether the agency should lower production as the coronavirus lowers demand.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Democrats ask Trump to suspend construction of border wall
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Join the Lone Star Prize
rows.standfirst: Lyda Hill Philanthropies will award a $10M grant opportunity for a long-term, transformative solution to improve the lives of Texans.

rows.title: MJ Hegar far outpaces Royce West in U.S. Senate fundraising, but both are far behind John Cornyn
rows.standfirst: The Texans’ campaigns are announcing their latest fundraising numbers ahead of an end-of-day deadline to disclose them to the Federal Election Commission.

rows.title: “They’re proud of me”: With a mask and a passion to help, lawyer keeps working in Mexican border city
rows.standfirst: An El Paso lawyer helps migrants in Juárez. A student struggles to focus while studying at home. A food pantry worker searches for a familiar face. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: Texas judge issues order that could greatly expand mail-in voting
rows.standfirst: A state district judge issued a temporary injunction expanding who can qualify for an absentee ballot for the upcoming elections. The decision faces certain appeal as Democrats and Republicans clash over voter access.

rows.title: TribCast: Forecasting what’s next with coronavirus and the 2021 legislative session
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Cassi and Ross about what’s coming up in the state’s response to the coronavirus pandemic, and the group does some forecasting for what the public health emergency could mean for the 2021 legislative session.

rows.title: Bracing for coronavirus but losing money every day, this East Texas hospital had to cut employees
rows.standfirst: Health care facilities are under financial pressure after a steep drop-off in lucrative surgeries, meant to free up hospital space and preserve protective equipment for the coronavirus outbreak.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Website launches to help essential workers find child care
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: More than 1 million people in Texas filed for unemployment relief in the last month
rows.standfirst: Texas unemployment claims continue to rise as Texans struggle to file. The Texas Workforce Commission is expanding its call centers, servers and staff, but many still face delays.

rows.title: Texas universities are getting millions in federal money to offset coronavirus losses. It won’t be enough, officials say.
rows.standfirst: Texas officials closed down campuses in early March and are losing millions of dollars as they pay students back for housing, parking and other unused services.

rows.title: She’s an undocumented immigrant, a taxpayer and an essential worker. But she won’t get a stimulus check.
rows.standfirst: About 8% of Texas workers are undocumented, and because they’re not eligible for stimulus payments, many are facing tough choices during the pandemic.

rows.title: This can’t be our new normal
rows.standfirst: When people ask me how my family is coping, I say we are fine. We’re in a house with plenty of food and reliable internet access. If my sons (a high schooler and a college student) need help with at-home learning, they meet with their teachers during Zoom office hours. Like everyone, we’re doing our best to get by. However, I also know the lessons are less engaging, less personalized and my kids can’t socialize the way they do at school. As a mother, I think to myself, this cannot become the “new normal.”

rows.title: Texas is running out of money to pay unemployment benefits. People will still get paid, but businesses may see tax hikes as a result.
rows.standfirst: Texas Workforce Commission officials say the state will run out of money in May or June. Other economists predict that could happen in as soon as three weeks.

rows.title: Texas requests federal funding to cover coronavirus testing for the uninsured
rows.standfirst: The federal funds became available in mid-March. Texas has more than 5 million uninsured residents, or about 18% of its population, a higher rate than any other state.

rows.title: Texas small-business owners scramble as federal relief fund runs out
rows.standfirst: Many businesses without accountants, lawyers or other professional help failed to get their applications in for the Paycheck Protection Program funds before the money was depleted.

rows.title: Federal judge orders Texas prison to provide hand sanitizer, face masks for inmates
rows.standfirst: The Houston judge issued a temporary order against the Texas Department of Criminal Justice at a geriatric prison after older inmates sued the prison system over its handling of the coronavirus.

rows.title: How Texas lawmakers are navigating the personal and professional during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Legislators are fielding calls about unemployment claims and small-business loans as they juggle steering their own businesses and careers through the disaster.

rows.title: Analysis: Coronavirus could threaten local property tax limits
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus disaster could have a side effect in a seemingly unrelated area: New limits on increases in local property taxes can be suspended when disasters strike. And epidemics, under state law, are disasters.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Judge opens door to expansion of voting by mail
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott discuss plans to reopen economy during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: The governor has cautioned it will be a “slow process” guided by public health concerns. Watch Friday’s news conference live at noon Central Time.

rows.title: As economic data lags, Texas reports 4.7% jobless rate for March
rows.standfirst: The figures predate the widespread business closures and layoffs that occurred in the wake of the pandemic. Analysts estimate the actual rate of jobless Texans is greater than 10%, which could be a record high.

rows.title: Texas’ unemployment rate has fallen by nearly half since the record high in April 2020
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus pandemic swiftly swept Texas into an economic recession, prompting millions to seek unemployment aid and complicating the state budget. Here’s a look at how the recovery is going.

rows.title: Laredo, a key Texas border crossing, uses strict coronavirus measures as it fears spread to rest of U.S.
rows.standfirst: With curfews, anti-gathering orders and a requirement to wear masks, Laredo has implemented some of the strictest protective measures in the nation.

rows.title: Medical offices are struggling during the pandemic. Texas health officials are proposing a $334 million lifeline.
rows.standfirst: The Texas Health and Human Services Commission sent the request to Gov. Greg Abbott and a panel of state legislators.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott announces team to restart the economy, loosens some restrictions
rows.standfirst: The reopening will happen in phases, Abbott said, and will be guided by data and doctors.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott keeps Texas classrooms closed for remainder of school year
rows.standfirst: Doctors and health experts say it isn’t safe to let students go back to their schools, the governor said at a news conference announcing executive orders intended to slowly reopen the Texas economy.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott relaxes ban on nonessential medical procedures, says courts will decide if abortions can proceed
rows.standfirst: Abbott’s original ban was intended to preserve medical resources. On Friday, he said Texas had ample hospital bed space and a strong supply chain of personal protective equipment.

rows.title: Texas officials project optimism on hospital capacity, medical resources
rows.standfirst: Concerns that Texas hospitals would be unable to accommodate a surge of COVID-19 patients seem to have been assuaged in recent days.

rows.title: Texas utility regulators have programs to prevent shutoffs during the pandemic. But some Texans are falling through the cracks.
rows.standfirst: Although some counties have moratoriums on disconnections, in most of the state customers need to apply for the benefit.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Neiman Marcus preparing to declare bankruptcy; thousands line up for food in Houston
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Is this rural community really Texas’ sickest county?
rows.standfirst: State data indicates that Donley County in the Panhandle has the highest coronavirus infection rate in Texas. But county Judge John Howard — also the only local doctor — believes that’s because he’s testing far more than other counties.

rows.title: Analysis: In an important election year, politics takes a back seat
rows.standfirst: The 2020 election year was already momentous, and then a pandemic broke out, demanding the full attention of the voters whom politicians depend on. Everything from how we vote to when we vote is now in question.

rows.title: Officials knew coronavirus could spread at the Houston Rodeo and proceeded with the event anyway
rows.standfirst: The Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo is the city’s largest annual event, attracting 2.5 million people and generating nearly $400 million. But officials pushed forward with this year’s 20-day event until there was a positive coronavirus case from community spread.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Most state parks reopen; National Guard to open new testing sites
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Questions about coronavirus? Ask Dr. Ben
rows.standfirst: Texas A&M University-Texarkana’s Dr. Benjamin Neuman regularly answers questions about the coronavirus from journalists around the world. He also takes the time to answer them from kids.

rows.title: Drive-thrus and free pencils: Texas plans for July elections with in-person voting
rows.standfirst: Other states may be shifting to increased mail-in voting, but Texas’ GOP leaders are fighting efforts to expand the practice. That leaves local elections officials to try to make polling places safe in a pandemic.

rows.title: Texas oil price plummets into the negatives as the coronavirus pandemic’s economic woes continue battering the state
rows.standfirst: It’s the lowest price for a barrel of crude since at least the 1980s and another sign, experts say, of rough economic times ahead — especially for Texas’ energy sector.

rows.title: Federal appeals court says Texas can block pill-induced abortions during pandemic
rows.standfirst: In March, Gov. Greg Abbott barred all procedures not “immediately medically necessary,” and the state’s attorney general declared that the restriction applied to abortions — sparking a weekslong court fight and prompting some women to seek abortions out of state.

rows.title: President Donald Trump says he’s temporarily halting immigration during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Trump tweeted Monday night that he will issue an executive order but gave few details about what it would do — or when he would issue it.

rows.title: T-Squared: Our new women’s health reporter and copy editor
rows.standfirst: Shannon Najmabadi will cover women’s health at The Texas Tribune, and Emily Goldstein is our new staff copy editor.

rows.title: Life after foster care was already tough. Now these Texans are facing the coronavirus pandemic, too.
rows.standfirst: As millions of Texans clamor for public benefits during the global health crisis, the pandemic has exposed gaps in support for young adults who have aged out of foster care. Many have experienced homelessness.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: U.S. Senate backs new round of economic aid; Dallas County extends stay-at-home order
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Dan Patrick says “there are more important things than living and that’s saving this country”
rows.standfirst: Patrick went on Fox News on Monday evening to defend comments he made last month where he said he would rather die from the widely spreading coronavirus than see the economy destroyed for his children and grandchildren.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott give an update on the state’s response to the novel coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Tuesday’s news conference comes a day after the governor announced plans for the Texas National Guard to mobilize more than 1,200 personnel for COVID-19 mobile testing teams. Watch Abbott’s live update from the state Capitol starting at 2 p.m. Central time.

rows.title: This North Texas mayor is trying to reopen businesses in Colleyville, bucking Abbott’s stay-at-home order
rows.standfirst: Colleyville Mayor Richard Newton appears to be the first mayor in Texas to move ahead with plans to relax stay-at-home orders aimed to curb the spread of the coronavirus.

rows.title: Texas oil regulators take no action on production
rows.standfirst: A day after oil prices crashed, The Texas Railroad Commission opted against taking action to impose limits on oil producers.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott’s task force to reopen the economy is packed with top business leaders — and donors
rows.standfirst: The task force features some of the most prominent and politically powerful business executives in the state. They’ll advise Abbott with the help of medical experts.

rows.title: Texas investigating meat processing plants over coronavirus outbreaks
rows.standfirst: The Department of State Health Services is looking into outbreaks at JBS Beef in Moore County and Tyson Foods in Shelby County.

rows.title: Trump campaign still owes El Paso more than $500,000 for a 2019 rally. City officials may sue to get the money.
rows.standfirst: City officials sent the campaign the most recent invoice in February. The mayor on Tuesday said the city should consider filing a lawsuit to recoup the money as it faces down a budget shortfall from the new coronavirus.

rows.title: Analysis: Energy isn’t the whole Texas economy, but it’s a critical piece
rows.standfirst: This week’s drop in crude oil prices signals trouble for state and local government budgets. Energy isn’t the biggest source of tax money in Texas, but the big one — the sales tax — is already falling.

rows.title: You might be protected from eviction until Aug. 23. Here’s how to find out.
rows.standfirst: A new database allows renters to search if their buildings are under a federal eviction moratorium due to COVID-19. But advocates note that even if you aren’t listed, you might still have protections.

rows.title: Texans in Congress look for ways to help as oil prices tank
rows.standfirst: While some companies can access small-business funds, the major stimulus that has made its way through Congress has no specific help for the energy sector. Members from Texas are looking for other ways to help.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: County jail population shrank by more than 10,000
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Webinar series to support businesses of all sizes
rows.standfirst: Comcast and industry experts explore critical topics facing today’s business community

rows.title: Coronavirus put her out of work, then debt collectors froze her savings account
rows.standfirst: Kim Boatswain’s tax refund could have helped her get through the coronavirus slowdown. But debt collectors seized it. There are few options for Texans like Boatswain whose money was taken just before the state temporarily banned such garnishments.

rows.title: Texas clinics resume abortion services as state acknowledges ban is no longer in place
rows.standfirst: A new order from Republican Gov. Greg Abbott that took effect Wednesday allows more procedures to resume in health care facilities that agree to reserve a certain number of beds for coronavirus patients and refrain from seeking scarce protective equipment from public sources.

rows.title: Oil prices collapsed, but that doesn’t mean Texans will get free gasoline
rows.standfirst: With most Texans staying at home and not driving, the demand for gas has fallen off. But refineries would stop producing before giving gas away for free.

rows.title: Harris County latest to mandate face masks as criticism mounts that the requirement is “government overreach”
rows.standfirst: GOP officials called it “tyranny” and “government overreach,” taking issue in particular with the $1,000 fine associated with violating the mask requirement.

rows.title: Federal appeals court stops earlier order, says Texas doesn’t have to give inmates hand sanitizer or face masks for now
rows.standfirst: The ruling temporarily halted a lower court’s order that was handed down after inmates at a geriatric prison sued the Texas prison system over its handling of the coronavirus.

rows.title: Texas will not release information about coronavirus clusters at state-run homes for Texans with disabilities
rows.standfirst: Residents’ families, restricted from visiting in an effort to stop the spread, are pleading for information. Even they aren’t being told how severe the outbreaks are where their loved ones live.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott promises far-reaching announcement on reopening Texas businesses, including restaurants, hair salons
rows.standfirst: Abbott said he is seeking approval from medical advisers on the business reopenings and that they will reopen under new standards to slow the spread of the coronavirus.

rows.title: Texas House Speaker Dennis Bonnen suggests ordering 5% budget cuts for state agencies
rows.standfirst: Bonnen raised the idea in a letter earlier this month to Gov. Greg Abbott and Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick.

rows.title: TribCast: Reopening the economy, testing in rural Texas and election woes
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Evan, Matthew and Emma about the slow efforts to reopen the Texas economy, a testing quandary in rural Texas and election administrators’ woes over the upcoming elections.

rows.title: Kim Olson’s departure from the Air Force hasn’t been a political liability. Will that change in 2020?
rows.standfirst: Olson retired from the Air Force amid a contracting scandal. Some Democrats worry the circumstances will make her vulnerable as she runs for a battleground U.S. House seat.

rows.title: “A victory every time”: Battling cancer while the world battles the coronavirus
rows.standfirst: A 5-year-old continues his cancer treatments. A couple watch the business they built wither. A small hospital treats its first coronavirus patient. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Prisons will increase testing; state files price gouging lawsuit over egg prices
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: 280,000 more Texans filed for unemployment last week as oil collapse and coronavirus precautions wallop state’s economy
rows.standfirst: The total number of out-of-work Texans is 1.3 million since mid-March as the state’s economy continues roiling from business closures, a troubled energy sector and corporate layoffs.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court sides with Abbott after judge halted his order restricting jail release
rows.standfirst: The high court did not weigh in on the arguments that Gov. Greg Abbott’s order went beyond his executive powers in a disaster. Instead, it ruled that the Harris County judges were the wrong plaintiffs.

rows.title: Trump signs order pausing immigration for 60 days, with exceptions
rows.standfirst: The order doesn’t apply to many categories of immigrants, but Immigrant advocates worry that the order is the beginning of even stricter measures.

rows.title: Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo sued over face mask requirement
rows.standfirst: The suit claims Hidalgo has exceeded her authority by implementing orders more restrictive than those of Gov. Greg Abbott, which take precedence.

rows.title: At Huston-Tillotson University, a stepping stone from poverty gets steeper
rows.standfirst: The historically black school in Austin moved online as coronavirus shut down college campuses. The loss of community is difficult for a school with a hands-on tradition of boosting students, many poor and the first in their families to attend college.

rows.title: As Congress rushed coronavirus aid to Texas business owners, some small companies fell through the cracks
rows.standfirst: Congress is preparing to send billions more to businesses. Some say the first round of money was depleted as larger enterprises beat smaller businesses to the punch.

rows.title: Congress approves another $484 billion to help people and businesses hit by coronavirus’ economic crisis
rows.standfirst: The bill will temporarily replenish about $320 billion into a forgivable loan fund earmarked for small businesses.

rows.title: Most Texas voters think coronavirus will be contained “in the next few months,” UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: Texas voters are concerned about the coronavirus. But most think the disease could be contained enough for a return to normal activities within a few months, according to the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Texas reports 22,806 cases and 593 deaths, releases online map of testing locations
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: In 50 Texas counties without cases, is it a lack of the coronavirus or a lack of testing?
rows.standfirst: In rural areas where the presence of the virus has yet to be confirmed, testing has been scarce — raising questions about whether the virus is lingering undetected.

rows.title: Calls spiked — then dropped. Domestic abuse survivors, at home with abusers during the pandemic, may be unable to get help.
rows.standfirst: Advocates worry that survivors are struggling to seek help because they’re stuck with their abusers at home due to stay-at-home orders.

rows.title: Harris County closing temporary medical center for overflow coronavirus patients without ever using it
rows.standfirst: Local leaders had planned for the center to be an overflow medical facility in case of a surge in COVID-19 cases.

rows.title: Everything we learned from the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune poll
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump leads Democrat Joe Biden by 5 points in the race for president in Texas, but voters give the president mixed grades on his handling of the pandemic and the economy. They think Gov. Greg Abbott is doing a better job.

rows.title: Rural Texas has struggled to get testing compared with big cities, but mobile testing sites could help
rows.standfirst: Smaller communities have also struggled to get tests because they were not prioritized by the government or are too cash-strapped to buy them from the private sector, which runs the majority of tests in Texas.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Poor ZIP codes in Harris County hit hardest by coronavirus, according to report
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Trump narrowly leads Biden in presidential race in Texas, UT/TT Poll finds
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump leads former Vice President Joe Biden by 5 points in the race for president in Texas, but voters give the president mixed grades on his handling of the pandemic and the economy.

rows.title: Texas voters: Gov. Greg Abbott is doing better on the economy and coronavirus than President Donald Trump
rows.standfirst: Even some Democrats who are dissatisfied with the president give good marks to Texas’ Republican governor, according to a University of Texas/Texas Tribune poll of the state’s voters.

rows.title: Only 23% of Texas registered voters approve of the job Congress is doing — and that’s an improvement over 18% in February
rows.standfirst: There’s no partisan split among Texas voters when it comes to assessing Congress’ performance: 53% of Democrats and 57% of Republicans disapprove of the job federal lawmakers are doing.

rows.title: Texas voters overwhelmingly approve of business closures, stay-at-home orders despite blow to state’s economy, says UT/TT poll
rows.standfirst: The poll results come as Gov. Greg Abbott prepares to announce his plans for reopening a wide range of Texas businesses.

rows.title: Meatpacking workers in Texas Panhandle have little power to avoid the coronavirus
rows.standfirst: A workforce of immigrants has long powered the massive JBS meatpacking plant in Cactus, where a cluster of coronavirus cases is under investigation. They’re risking their lives each shift in the county with the state’s highest known infection rate.

rows.title: Before Texas can safely reopen its economy, health experts say these four things must happen
rows.standfirst: Pressure to return to normalcy is building, but health experts say even gradual steps will increase the number of COVID-19 cases. First, they say, Texas needs more testing and contact tracing.

rows.title: Analysis: A governor balancing noisy resistance to staying at home with the rest of his political base
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott faces pushback toward stay-at-home policy within his own party, but a larger number of Republicans are willing to take measures to protect public health.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Baylor says it will resume in-person teaching this fall and open its dorms
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Watch Gov. Greg Abbott detail plans to reopen Texas economy during coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Abbott is expected to lay out how businesses will resume operations while minimizing the spread of COVID-19, the illness caused by the new coronavirus. Watch live starting at 2:30 p.m. Central time.

rows.title: Texas will bounce back from this “double-whammy tsunami”
rows.standfirst: While the pandemic and oil glut create a double dose of devastation, three Texas A&M scholars tell Chancellor John Sharp that they see new economic opportunities rising from the rubble.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott to let restaurants, movie theaters and malls open with limited capacity Friday
rows.standfirst: The businesses must limit occupancy to no more than 25%. Abbott said the state’s stay-at-home order “has done its job to slow the growth of COVID-19.”

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says Harris County can’t impose fine over face mask order
rows.standfirst: County Judge Lina Hidalgo’s order, which carries a penalty of up to $1,000, drew harsh criticism from GOP officials and members of law enforcement.

rows.title: As businesses prepare to reopen, workers weigh COVID-19 risk against the need for a paycheck
rows.standfirst: If a business reopens and an employee chooses not to return to work, they become ineligible for unemployment, according to the Texas Workforce Commission.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: Southwest Airlines announces first quarterly loss in nearly 10 years
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: Analysis: Reopening Texas during a pandemic, cautiously and slowly
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott wants to reopen the state and to get the economy going. But he also wants to avoid widening the spread of the coronavirus. Texans are about to find out whether it’s possible to have it both ways.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court extends moratorium on evictions until May 18
rows.standfirst: Housing advocates say they are still concerned about cases of harassment and the longterm housing safety of vulnerable Texans.

rows.title: TribCast, special edition: Our pollsters analyze the latest UT/TT Poll on coronavirus in Texas
rows.standfirst: In this edition of the TribCast, Ross talks to pollsters Joshua Blank and Daron Shaw about the latest University of Texas/Texas Tribune Poll, focused on the coronavirus pandemic and how voters and governments are responding to it.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott ends self-quarantine mandate for travelers from Louisiana
rows.standfirst: Starting Friday, road and air travelers entering Texas from Louisiana will no longer have to self-quarantine for 14 days.

rows.title: Texas restaurants, retailers and other businesses can reopen Friday. Here’s the rules they have to follow.
rows.standfirst: Parties of six or less, disposable menus and limited capacity are among the new rules businesses will follow if they open this Friday.

rows.title: Black Texans already face health care disparities. The coronavirus is making it worse.
rows.standfirst: As the coronavirus spreads, black people are less likely to have access to proper health care and more likely to have health issues that make the virus more dangerous.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: State’s beaches set to reopen Friday
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: With little certainty and a lot of hope, Texas restaurants and retailers navigate new rules as they prepare to reopen
rows.standfirst: After weeks of limited business operations, the first wave of the Texas economy will reopen on Friday. The service and entertainment industries are preparing for new rules even as they face an uncertain future.

rows.title: Federal government sued for denying stimulus checks to Americans married to undocumented immigrants
rows.standfirst: The Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund, is alleging that a provision in the $2.2 trillion stimulus package known as the CARES Act that denies the benefit to mixed-status families in unconstitutional.

rows.title: Texas voters sue over age restrictions for mail-in ballots
rows.standfirst: The voters — all between the ages of 18 and 28 — want the courts to rule that the state’s age restriction for voting by mail, which limits eligibility to those 65 and older, violates constitutional protections.

rows.title: Texas sending restaurant and retail employees back to work without child care
rows.standfirst: Restaurant, retail and movie theater workers may be called back to work as soon as Friday. But licensed child care remains open only for children of “essential” workers.

rows.title: Health experts give Abbott’s plan to reopen Texas mixed reviews, warn state should revive stay-at-home order if surge emerges
rows.standfirst: Many health experts said the governor was right to open the economy in phases, but some cautioned that his timeline was too quick.

rows.title: TribCast: How Texas plans to reopen businesses during the coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Cassi, Matthew and Ross about the phased reopening of Texas businesses and what that could mean for Texans who must return to work in a pandemic.

rows.title: “This ain’t the time to follow rules”: Texas A&M wants to run human coronavirus tests in its animal labs
rows.standfirst: A&M officials say they have the largest public lab capacity in the state, but the federal government won’t let them use it for humans.

rows.title: In Houston’s Chinatown, restaurants plan to feed front-line workers during the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Restaurant owners aim to give 10,000 meals to frontline workers. A boy with cancer wants a mohawk. An East Texas town prepares to reopen some businesses. In this weekly series, Texans from across the state share stories about how they’re navigating life during the COVID-19 pandemic.

rows.title: As Texas Gov. Greg Abbott phases in reopening, some in his party are testing his rules
rows.standfirst: Abbott’s instinct so far has been mostly to deescalate, staving off confrontations that could hobble the careful course he is charting.

rows.title: Coronavirus in Texas: State sees highest single-day death toll from COVID-19
rows.standfirst: Our staff is closely tracking developments on the new coronavirus in Texas. Check here for live updates.

rows.title: As unemployment roils the state, some Texans have given up on trying to get help
rows.standfirst: 254,199 Texans filed for unemployment last week — bringing the total number of claims to over 1.5 million in six weeks.

rows.title: Texas A&M and University of Texas systems expect to reopen in the fall, and A&M says it will play football
rows.standfirst: Texas Tech University also says it’s planning for a return to campus for the upcoming school year.

rows.title: Texas still won’t say which nursing homes have COVID-19 cases. Families are demanding answers.
rows.standfirst: Citing a state medical privacy law, Texas is refusing to release the names of long-term care facilities where residents have died from COVID-19, even as those case numbers soar and families plead for information.

rows.title: In West Texas, volunteers manufacture medical supplies and amateur pilots deliver to remote hospitals
rows.standfirst: A volunteer air force of more than 1,000 amateur aviators has come together to transport essential medical supplies in a part of the state where the cities are far-flung and the roads are notoriously dangerous from oil-related traffic.

rows.title: Texas relaxes guidelines to allow unemployment benefits for workers who don’t or can’t return to work during pandemic
rows.standfirst: The expanded qualifications now include people who don’t have access to child care because schools and day cares are closed to everyone but the children of essential workers.

rows.title: Balancing “caution and pent-up demand”: Texans face health risks and financial woes as state’s battered economy slowly reopens
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott has received mixed reviews for reopening businesses during the coronavirus pandemic. While some Texans aren’t eager to venture out, others feel a responsibility to support local enterprises.

rows.title: Attorney general’s office warns local officials that barber shops, hair salons and gyms still can’t reopen
rows.standfirst: After Gov. Greg Abbott announced he would reopen large parts of the economy Friday, some local leaders argued that his orders were vague. Top state attorneys disagree.

rows.title: Texas reports record coronavirus deaths the day before stores open. But Gov. Greg Abbott sees hope in other metrics.
rows.standfirst: Abbott is looking at two figures: the percentage of tests in the state that come back positive and the percentage of patients with COVID-19 who are hospitalized.
